cover.headline: Trophy hotels, a pile of cash and Colombo apartments, at a price that already assumes the worst of 2026
cover.lead: ITC Hotels, demerged from ITC in Jan-2025, owns some of India's best city luxury hotels and manages ~8,600 more keys for others: 156 hotels and 14,372 keys in all, plus ITC Ratnadipa and the Sapphire Residences apartments in Colombo. Q1FY27 revenue rose 15% (hotels +10%) and EBITDA 19% despite the West Asia shock. The street values it on **EV/EBITDA of the hotels on FY28E (22-25x)** plus cash and the apartments; all twelve standing views are Buy (median target ₹210). We are more cautious on growth (FY28E EBITDA ~9% below the two published estimates) but the stock has fallen further than its peers: it trades at 17.4x our FY28E hotel EBITDA against a post-listing median of 24.3x, while hotel peers sit 16% below theirs. Applying the house rule gives **20.5x Sep-28E hotel EBITDA** and a sum of the parts of **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with BUY.** The P/E cross-check agrees (₹211); the DCF (₹115) does not. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.p: ITC Maurya, ITC Grand Chola, ITC Maratha, ITC Gardenia and their peers earn a RevPAR 37% above the luxury-upscale market (FY26) and ~35% hotel margins; the restaurants (Bukhara, Dum Pukht, Avartana) make F&B ~39% of hotel revenue.

arguments.h: Growth is ordinary, fees are small
arguments.p: Hotels grew 10% in FY26 and in Q1FY27; room rates only +6% and +4%. Fees (₹173 cr, +28%) are ~4% of hotel revenue. We model revenue +{{F.salesGrowth.0|pct}} / +{{F.salesGrowth.1|pct}} / +{{F.salesGrowth.2|pct}} and EPS growth of ~13% a year (FY26-29E, before one-offs).

~₹3,175 cr of net cash and ₹1,240 cr of unsold Colombo apartments (~13% of the market value together), no debt. But ROE is ~7% and pre-tax ROCE ~11%: the moat protects margins, not returns. BAT still holds 6.28% after selling ~9% in Dec-2025.

arguments.h: Valuation: the stock de-rated more than the sector
arguments.p: At ₹164 the market pays ~15.8x Sep-28E hotel EBITDA once cash and the apartments are valued our way; ITC Hotels' trailing multiple is 20% below its post-listing median vs 16% for IHCL, EIH and Lemon Tree. Our 20.5x is still below the street's 22-25x. We would buy below ~₹180.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): the first quarter without the April shock; watch room rates, the Kumarakom renovation and the Ahmedabad (GHK) integration.
The Oct-Mar peak season: weddings, MICE and inbound travel after the West Asia conflict.
Sapphire Residences handovers and Sri Lankan property taxes; the Sri Lankan rupee.
BAT's remaining 6.28%: a further sale would add supply; a clean exit would remove the overhang.
Use of the cash: more acquisitions (management calls itself well placed for value-accretive deals), a higher dividend, or more owned builds.

sections.title: A luxury hotel owner with a growing fee business on the side, and a Colombo apartment project to sell down

blocks.p: ITC Hotels earns money three ways. **It owns hotels** (~5,700 keys, ~40% of operating keys), mostly large luxury city hotels such as ITC Maurya and ITC Grand Bharat (Delhi), ITC Maratha and ITC Grand Central (Mumbai), ITC Grand Chola (Chennai), ITC Gardenia (Bengaluru), ITC Sonar and Royal Bengal (Kolkata), ITC Kohenur (Hyderabad), ITC Grand Goa and ITC Mughal (Agra), plus ITC Ratnadipa in Colombo. The large ITC hotels are franchised into Marriott's Luxury Collection for global distribution. These hotels make most of the revenue and EBITDA and carry almost all the capital. **It manages hotels for other owners** (~8,600 keys, 60%) under Welcomhotel, Fortune, Storii, Mementos and WelcomHeritage for a fee: ₹173 cr in FY26, ~4% of hotel revenue. **It sells apartments** at Sapphire Residences in Colombo (₹211 cr in FY26). At 30-Jun-2026 it had 156 operating hotels with 14,372 keys and 77 more (7,962 keys) signed; the goal is 250 hotels and 22,000+ keys by 2031.

blocks.callout: **Why the mix matters:** the owned hotels are where the value, the capital and the returns problem sit (₹11,658 cr of equity earning ~7%); the managed hotels are where the growth sits (74 of 77 pipeline hotels are managed). The Colombo apartments are a one-off cash release, not a business.

sections.title: Fifty years inside ITC, twenty months as a listed company: the demerger, the BAT sell-down and what it does to the numbers

blocks.p: ITC ran its hotels as a division for fifty years (the company marked its 50th year in May-2026). In 2023 it decided to demerge them: ITC Hotels Ltd was incorporated on 28-Jul-2023, the demerger took effect on 1-Jan-2025, ITC kept 40% and ITC's shareholders received one ITC Hotels share for every ten ITC shares. The shares listed on 29-Jan-2025. For investors three things follow. **(1) A short history:** only two full years of accounts and ~20 months of prices, so our multiple history starts after listing (valuation chapter). **(2) Restated comparatives:** the FY25 accounts restate the hotels business only from incorporation, so Screener's "FY24" is ~8 months and is not used. **(3) A shifting register:** BAT's Tobacco Manufacturers (India), which received its shares as an ITC shareholder, has been selling (12.21% at Mar-25, 6.28% at Mar-26), and HCL Capital bought 7.08%.

sections.title: A fourth year of demand ahead of supply, but growth is slowing and the 2026 travel shock re-priced hotel stocks

blocks.p: Indian hotels are in their best cycle in twenty years: since Covid, domestic travel, weddings, conferences and corporate demand have grown faster than new rooms, lifting occupancy and room rates. ICRA (29-Sep-26) expects FY27 industry revenue growth of 7-9% (FY26 ~11%), with occupancy of 72-74% and an average rate of ₹8,600-8,800. HVS Anarock's July-2026 monitor put the Jun-2026 average rate at ₹7,900-8,100 (+10-12%) and occupancy at 64-66% (+3-5 pp); branded signings (28,268 keys in H1 CY26) run about four times openings (6,269), so supply will pick up from 2027-28. The shock of 2026 was the West Asia conflict: air travel disruption, weak foreign arrivals and higher fuel and food costs. ITC Hotels called April 2026 "broad-based demand softness"; May and June recovered.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** the cycle reaches ITC Hotels through occupancy, F&B and fees, but its luxury rate growth is already slower than the market's and its earnings growth (~10-12% a year in our forecast) is ordinary. The stock is a quality-at-a-price story, not a growth story.

sections.title: The owned luxury hotels make most of the money: RevPAR ~1.3x the industry, ~35% margins, but rate growth has slowed to mid-single digits

blocks.p: The hotels segment (everything except the Colombo apartments) earned ₹3,928 cr of revenue and ₹1,360 cr of EBITDA in FY26 (34.6%). Rooms were ₹1,986 cr (+10%), food and beverage ₹1,535 cr (+8%; ITC's restaurants, Bukhara, Dum Pukht, Avartana, are a real draw for weddings and banquets), management fees ₹173 cr (+28%) and other income from operations ₹234 cr. The owned hotels ran at an average room rate (ARR) of ~₹13,200 (+6%) and RevPAR of ~₹9,700 (+10%), a 37% premium to the luxury-upscale market (CoStar). In Q1FY27 rooms grew 8% (rate +4%, occupancy +290 bps to 74%) after a weak April (West Asia conflict); F&B +11%, fees +35%; the margin rose 125 bps to 31.3%.

blocks.callout: **Our read:** these are some of India's best hotels (ITC Maurya, ITC Grand Chola, ITC Maratha, ITC Gardenia, ITC Grand Bharat), and the RevPAR premium is real. But the growth engine is modest: FY26 room rates rose 6% and Q1FY27 4%, and most growth in the owned hotels now comes from occupancy and food. We forecast rooms +9% / +11% / +9% (FY27-29E, incl. ~200 acquired keys at Ahmedabad and Kumarakom and ~220 new keys at Bhubaneswar and Puri) and a hotel margin of 35.3% → 36.5%.

sections.title: Management fees are the growth engine: ₹173 cr in FY26 (+28%), ~4% of hotel revenue, aiming for 2.5x FY25 by FY30

blocks.p: ITC Hotels runs ~8,600 keys for other owners under Welcomhotel, Fortune, Storii, Mementos and WelcomHeritage (60% of operating keys) and has 74 managed hotels with 7,200+ keys signed. It signed a record 33 hotels (3,300+ keys) in FY26 and 8 more in Q1FY27. Fees were ₹173 cr in FY26 (+28%) and ₹49 cr in Q1FY27 (+35%). The target is 2.5x FY25 fees by FY30 (~₹340 cr), and ~15,000 managed keys by 2031 (12% a year). Fees need no capital and carry almost no cost, which is why every brokerage sees them as the re-rating story.

pair.title: Fees grow ~20% a year in our forecast
Brands: Fortune and Welcomhotel carry the pipeline

blocks.callout: **But keep it in proportion:** even at our ~20% a year, fees reach ₹306 cr in FY29E, 5.8% of hotel revenue. IHCL earns ~4x as much in fees (₹685 cr in FY26). Most of ITC Hotels' managed keys are midscale (Fortune, Welcomhotel) in tier-2 and tier-3 cities, where fees per key are low. Even if fees carried no cost at all, they would be only ~16% of FY29E EBITDA: the owned hotels remain the business.

sections.title: Colombo: ITC Ratnadipa now makes money; Sapphire Residences has ~₹1,240 cr of apartments still to sell

blocks.p: ITC's biggest single project was a mixed-use development on the Galle Face seafront in Colombo, owned by WelcomHotels Lanka (100%): **ITC Ratnadipa** (352 keys, opened in FY25, EBITDA-positive in FY26 and again in Q1FY27, with the city's highest RevPAR) and **Sapphire Residences** (132 apartments designed with Philippe Starck's YOO). Handovers started in Q3FY26: the real-estate segment booked ₹211 cr of revenue and ₹64 cr of EBITDA in FY26 and ₹38 cr / ₹11 cr in Q1FY27. Sapphire Residences revenue is recognised on handover (from Q3FY26); FY26 real-estate development cost Rs138. The unsold stock (₹1,240 cr of inventory at cost at Mar-2026) is the swing item: the AR FY26 says elevated Sri Lankan real-estate taxes have tempered sales momentum, and the Sri Lankan rupee's fall cut equity by ₹210 cr through OCI in Q1FY27 alone.

pair.title: Apartment handovers: lumpy
We expect ₹160-180 cr a year of handovers

blocks.callout: **How we value it:** apartment EBITDA is not a recurring hotel profit, so it gets no hotel multiple. We value the unsold inventory at 80% of book (₹992 cr, ~₹5 a share; bull 90%, bear 70%) for time and Sri Lankan sales risk, and keep the margin on units we expect to hand over by Sep-28E in our net cash.

blocks.callout: **Verdict: a narrow moat.** Nobody can rebuild ITC Maurya or ITC Grand Chola at today's land and construction costs, and the food franchise is real. But a moat should show up in returns, and here it does not yet: ~7% ROE on book equity. The moat protects margins; it has not produced high returns on the capital tied up in it.

sections.title: Two full years as a listed company: revenue +16%, EBITDA +18% in FY26, helped by Colombo apartment sales; margins steady at ~34-35%

blocks.p: ITC Hotels has only two full years of its own accounts. FY25 revenue was ₹3,560 cr and EBITDA (operating profit before other income) ₹1,211 cr; FY26 revenue rose 16% to ₹4,139 cr and EBITDA 18% to ₹1,424 cr. About a third of that growth came from a new and lumpy source: ₹211 cr of revenue and ₹64 cr of EBITDA from handing over apartments at Sapphire Residences in Colombo (the "real estate" segment). The hotels alone grew 10% (₹3,928 cr) and their margin rose ~0.5 point to 34.6%. Reported profit was ₹817 cr after an ₹80 cr exceptional charge (new labour codes ₹54 cr; cyclone Ditwah damage in Sri Lanka ₹26 cr); before it, profit rose ~39%, also helped by ~₹125 cr more treasury income on the cash ITC handed over. Screener's FY24 column covers only ~8 months (from the company's incorporation on 28-Jul-2023), so the 60% "growth" in FY25 is an accounting artefact, not growth.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** the hotel business is solid but not fast-growing: ~10% revenue growth with ~34-35% margins. The profit line was flattered in FY26 by two things that will not repeat at the same pace: apartment handovers in Colombo and a jump in interest income on the cash ITC handed over. The honest yardstick is return on capital: on Screener's numbers ITC Hotels earns a pre-tax ROCE of ~11% and an ROE of ~7% on ₹11,658 cr of equity, because the owned luxury hotels carry a very large asset base.

sections.title: Q1FY27: revenue +15% (hotels +10%), EBITDA +19%, profit +36% in a quarter hit by West Asia

blocks.p: Results on 16-Jul-2026: consolidated revenue ₹936 cr (+15%), of which hotels ₹898 cr (+10%) and Sapphire Residences ₹38 cr; EBITDA ₹292 cr (+19%), hotel margin 31.3% (+125 bps); other income ₹59 cr; profit ₹182 cr (+36%). April 2026 demand softness across key markets from the West Asia conflict (air travel, weak foreign arrivals); swift recovery in May-June. The company does not give numerical revenue or margin guidance and, as far as we could find, holds no earnings calls; its stated targets are 2.5x FY25 management fees by FY30, 250 hotels and 22,000+ keys by 2031, and capex of 10-12% of cumulative revenue.

sections.title: Cash-rich and lightly invested so far; capex is now rising (acquisitions, Delhi and Vizag) and returns stay low

blocks.p: ITC Hotels turned 78% of FY26 EBITDA into operating cash (₹1,110 cr of ₹1,424 cr) and spent only ₹410 cr on fixed assets (₹386 cr in FY25), so cash and investments grew. It paid its first dividend (₹1 a share, ₹208 cr) for FY26. Spending is now stepping up: a luxury resort at Kumarakom (Kerala; ₹205 cr enterprise value) bought in May-2026, Welcomhotel Ahmedabad (GHK, enterprise value ₹155 cr) agreed in Jul-2026, a ₹326.5 cr land premium for a hotel at Yashobhoomi in New Delhi, a ₹328 cr hotel at Visakhapatnam, and projects at Puri and Bhubaneswar. Management's yardstick is 10-12% of cumulative revenue for operating capex, renovations and new builds (8-10% in the May-2026 deck). The managed (fee) side needs almost no capital: 60% of operating keys are managed and the target is ~15,000 managed keys by 2031.

sections.title: No debt, ~₹3,175 cr of net cash and ₹1,240 cr of unsold Colombo apartments: about 13% of the market value sits outside the hotels

blocks.p: At Mar-2026 ITC Hotels had **₹3,250 cr of cash, deposits and investments** (₹766 cr of cash and bank balances, ₹826 cr of mutual funds, ₹1,004 cr of bonds and listed associates, ₹529 cr of long bank deposits) and no bank debt; lease liabilities were ₹74 cr. Net cash was therefore ~₹3,175 cr (~₹15 a share), including ₹126 cr of associates at book (International Travel House 48.96%, a JV in WelcomHeritage). Screener shows only ₹2,721 cr of cash and investments because the long deposits sit in "other assets"; our model adds them back. The second large item is **₹1,240 cr of inventory**: the unsold apartments at Sapphire Residences, Colombo, carried at cost. They turn into cash only as buyers take handover (₹211 cr of revenue in FY26, ₹38 cr in Q1FY27). Equity is ₹11,658 cr, mostly hotels carried at ITC's historical book value.

sections.title: Ownership: ITC 39.85%; BAT halved its stake, foreign funds fell from 25% to 12% and Indian funds and retail took the shares

blocks.p: ITC Ltd holds 39.85% (83 cr shares) and is the only promoter. At the demerger BAT's entities received ~15.3% (pro rata to their ITC stake). On 5-Dec-2025 BAT sold ~9% (18.75 cr shares at an average ₹205.65, ~₹3,856 cr) to buyers including ADIA, HCL Capital, Nippon India MF and Vanguard, calling the stake 'not a strategic holding'; it kept 6.28% through Tobacco Manufacturers (India), and we found no further sale by 30-Sep-2026. That is why the FII share fell from 25.5% (Sep-25) to 16.1% (Dec-25) and 11.6% (Jun-26), while the 'public' line (which includes BAT's residual stake and HCL Capital) rose to 24.5%. LIC (8.70%) and SUUTI (4.68%) came with their ITC holdings. 22.9 lakh shareholders at Jun-2026, most of them small ITC holders who received shares in the demerger.

sections.title: Our forecasts: EBITDA ₹1,572 / 1,779 / 1,970 cr (FY27-29E), 3% below the street for FY27E and ~9% below for FY28E

blocks.p: We build the hotels from four streams (rooms, F&B, fees, others) and treat the Colombo apartments separately. Hotel revenue grows 9.9% / 11.0% / 9.5% (FY27-29E): rooms +9% / +11% / +9%, F&B +9% / +10% / +9%, fees +25% / +20% / +18%. The hotel margin rises from 34.6% (FY26) to 35.3% / 36.0% / 36.5%. Apartment revenue falls to ₹160 cr in FY27E and ₹180 cr a year after, at a 30% margin. Other income is built on the cash (~6.75-7% yield plus associates): ₹230 / 255 / 285 cr. Tax and minorities 26.8%. EPS ₹4.74 / 5.45 / 6.13.

pair.title: EBITDA: we are below the street for FY28E
Fees grow fastest but stay small

blocks.callout: **Why we are below the street for FY28E:** the street (ICICI Direct, Choice) has revenue rising ~15-16% in FY28E; we have 11.1%. Room rates rose only 4% in Q1FY27 and Nomura already cut its rate growth assumption to ~7% a year; the acquisitions (Kumarakom 72 keys, Ahmedabad 130 keys) and Puri/Bhubaneswar add ~2-3% to revenue, not 5%. Our margins are close to the street's (FY28E 35.8% vs 35.8-36.7%). If the street is right on revenue, our FY28E EBITDA is ~9% too low and our target ~₹220 (same multiple).

sections.title: The street: twelve Buys, targets ₹195-235 (median ₹210), on 22-25x FY28E hotel EBITDA plus the Colombo apartments and cash

blocks.p: Twelve brokers had a standing view on 30-Sep-2026, all Buy or Outperform where a rating is stated, with targets of ₹195-235 (median ₹210, mean ~₹213) against a price of ₹164. After the Q1FY27 results (16-Jul-2026) ICICI Securities raised its target to ₹235, Choice to ₹210 (from ₹190), ICICI Direct kept ₹220 (22x FY28E), Macquarie cut to ₹210 (from ₹220); Investec started at ₹201 (16-Sep) and Jefferies reiterated ₹210 on 23x FY28E (22-Sep). The May-2026 notes after the West Asia shock (Nomura ₹195, Elara ₹197, PhillipCapital ₹200, JM ₹225, Ambit ₹225) still stand. The pattern is telling: targets were cut from ₹230-253 in January (Nomura, JM, Elara) to ~₹195-235, multiples from 25-30x to 22-25x, yet the stock fell further. Bulls argue the luxury hotels are irreplaceable, the managed pipeline lifts margins and returns, and Colombo is now profitable. No note we found adjusted for the low return on capital or the BAT overhang.

exhibit.title: Critiques we take seriously
head: Argument
rows: Growth is ordinary: hotels grew 10% in FY26 and Q1FY27, room rates only 6% and 4%; the street's FY28E revenue (+15-16% in ICICI Direct and Choice) needs a big step-up.
Returns are low: ROE ~7% and pre-tax ROCE ~11% on ₹11,658 cr of equity; the cash pile earns ~7% and dilutes returns further.
The apartment sales in Colombo flatter FY26 growth (₹211 cr revenue) and are lumpy (₹38 cr in Q1FY27); Sri Lankan taxes slowed sales and the currency hits book value.
Overhang: BAT still holds 6.28% and calls it non-strategic; the stock fell 19% in 2026 to 30-Sep.
Fee business is small: ₹173 cr of fees vs IHCL's ₹685 cr; most managed hotels are midscale in smaller cities.
Disclosure: no earnings calls and no numerical guidance, so the street relies on decks and the AGM.

Bull case: irreplaceable city luxury hotels, a 33-37% RevPAR premium, ~₹3,175 cr of net cash plus ~₹1,240 cr of apartments to sell (~13% of the market value together), and an asset-light pipeline that lifts margins.
exhibit.source: Broker notes, filings and press to 30-Sep-2026; GAM Research

blocks.h: How the street values ITC Hotels

blocks.p: Every house that discloses a method values ITC Hotels on **EV/EBITDA of the hotel business** on FY28E (some on Dec-27E or Mar-28E), and the sum-of-the-parts versions add Sapphire Residences at about 1x its net asset value plus net cash: ICICI Direct 22x FY28E (₹1,936 cr EBITDA, Sapphire NAV ₹1,175 cr), Choice 22x FY28E hospitality EBITDA with the apartments at 0x, Jefferies and Nomura 23x FY28E (Nomura: a ~10% discount to IHCL), JM Financial 25x Mar-28E, ICICI Securities 25x Dec-27E (May note). We do the same on Sep-28E EBITDA, the 12-month-forward year the market will look at in September 2027.

pair.title: Hotels are ~90% of the value
Target and cross-checks vs the share price

blocks.p: House rule: start from the stock's own one-year-forward EV/EBITDA, adjust for how far the sector had moved against its own history by 30-Sep-2026, then test growth, peers, returns and the street. Three choices follow the settled rules. (1) **Window.** ITC Hotels listed on 29-Jan-25; there is no earlier price. Following the recently-listed rule we skip the listing months (Feb-Mar 2025, when index funds and ITC holders who did not want a hotel stock sold and before the first stand-alone annual results) and start on 1-Apr-25: 79 weekly closes to 30-Sep-2026. (2) **Same-window sector move.** The peers' move is measured against their own medians over the same window, not five years. The hotel peer set is IHCL's: IHCL, EIH and Lemon Tree; Chalet is excluded as in IHCL's report (₹163 cr of flat-sale EBITDA in its trailing numbers) and shown as a sensitivity. Three usable peers remain, the minimum we accept; we say so plainly. (3) **Hotel EV.** EV is market value less net cash (latest March balance sheet published by each date) less the apartment inventory at 80% of book, divided by next-year hotel EBITDA (FY27E for Apr-25 to Mar-26 dates, FY28E after), consistent with the SOTP; the consolidated version gives 24.2x.

Hotel stocks in India have always traded above what a ~12% cost of equity justifies on 10-12% growth; buyers of ITC Hotels are paying for a long runway, not for the next three years.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a fine hotel company at a fair-to-cheap price after a 20% de-rating

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** some of India's best city luxury hotels, a RevPAR premium of ~37% to the market, a growing fee stream (+35% in Q1FY27), ~₹3,175 cr of net cash (Mar-26) and ₹1,240 cr of Colombo apartments to sell, with ITC as the anchor shareholder. Earnings should grow ~12-14% a year (FY26-29E, before one-offs). What you are not buying: high returns (ROE ~7%) or fast growth.

**What you are paying:** 17.4x one-year-forward hotel EV/EBITDA (its own median since Apr-2025 is 24.3x) and 30.1x our FY28E EPS. The stock fell 20% against its own trailing-multiple median, more than the peers' 16%. On the street's method, our inputs and the house rule, the target is {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): a BUY. The rating rests on the multiple: the market pays only ~15.8x Sep-28E hotel EBITDA today, and the DCF does not support the price at a 12.2% discount rate.

sections.title: Glossary

exhibit.title: Terms used in this report
head: Term
What it means
rows: A company splits off a business into a new listed company; the parent's shareholders receive shares in it. ITC Hotels was demerged from ITC Ltd on 1-Jan-2025 (1 share for every 10 ITC shares).
Hotel rooms (each room has a key). Operating keys are open; pipeline keys are signed but not yet open.
Rooms sold ÷ rooms available in the period.
Average room rate: room revenue ÷ rooms sold.
Revenue per available room = occupancy × average room rate. The main measure of a hotel's pricing power.
How far a hotel's RevPAR is above the market's (here the luxury, upper-upscale and upscale market measured by CoStar).
Hotels ITC Hotels owns; it books all their revenue and costs and carries the capital.
Hotels owned by others and run (or branded) by ITC Hotels for a fee; only the fee is ITC Hotels' revenue.
Base fee (share of revenue) plus incentive fee (share of profit) from managed hotels.
A Marriott International brand; the large ITC hotels are franchised into it for global distribution and loyalty.
Branded apartments next to ITC Ratnadipa in Colombo; revenue is booked when an apartment is handed over.
Meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions: group business for hotels.
Operating profit before depreciation, interest, tax and other income. We use the company's definition (audited accounts).
Enterprise value (market value less net cash; here also less the Colombo apartment inventory) ÷ EBITDA; share price ÷ earnings per share.
Sum of the parts: each business valued separately, then added up, plus net cash.
Half of FY28E plus half of FY29E: the 12-month-forward earnings the market will look at in September 2027.
How far peers' trailing EV/EBITDA on 30-Sep-2026 sat below (or above) their own medians over the same window as our own history (from 1-Apr-2025).
Other comprehensive income: gains and losses that go straight to equity, here mainly currency translation of the Sri Lankan subsidiary.
Return on equity (profit ÷ shareholders' equity) and return on capital employed (operating profit ÷ equity plus debt).
Discounted cash flow valuation; WACC is the required annual return used to discount future cash (here the cost of equity, 12.2%, as ITC Hotels has no debt).
